message.content: At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈0.1 atm), water’s freezing (melting) point is slightly below the standard 0 °C.  According to the water phase diagram, the melting point at 10 kPa is roughly **–2 °C** (about –1.9 °C to –2.1 °C depending on the source).  This reflects the negative slope of the ice‑water equilibrium line: as pressure decreases, the freezing point rises a little, but at 10 kPa it is still a couple of degrees below 0 °C.
